case_analysis.thread_summary: This single internal message (2024-09-02) from an Allion consultant ([PERSON]) to a colleague ([PERSON]) provides answers to relay to a customer ([COMPANY], contact [PERSON]) regarding two SIG registration questions. The first concerns whether selecting 'Complete the Submission' permanently locks an additional model's registration content. The second concerns a deprecation warning on an existing registration (D063816) containing the soon-to-be-discontinued GLS 1.0 profile, and its planned 2025/2/1 invalidation (Withdrawal).
all_questions_found: If 'Complete the Submission' is selected when finalizing an additional model registration, does that mean no further corrections or changes can be made to that registration?
Is there a way to correct or change an additional model's registration content after 'Complete the Submission' has been executed?
What is the expected impact of the warning that additional registrations under DID D063816 will no longer be possible after 2025/2/1, and is there a workaround?
Will products already registered under D063816 before 2025/2/1 remain sellable after the DID becomes invalid?
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Two SIG registration/listing topics are addressed. First, after 'Complete the Submission' for an additional model, direct edits aren't possible, but the customer can request deletion (before the model's Publish Date) and re-register with corrected content. Second, DID D063816 contains GLS (Glucose Service) 1.0, a profile being deprecated by SIG on 2025/2/1; because this unused profile wasn't removed by the BQTF at original registration, the entire D063816 registration becomes invalid (Withdrawal) on that date, with no remedy via additional registration to the existing DID - only additional registrations completed under the Product List before 2025/1/31 remain valid and sellable thereafter.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: For the submission question, the consultant distinguishes between 'cannot edit directly' and 'cannot effectively change at all' - a delete-then-re-register path (bounded by the Publish Date) provides the effective correction mechanism. For the D063816 question, the consultant traces the warning to its root cause (an unremoved deprecated profile from the original registration), determines that the deprecation date triggers full Withdrawal of the DID (not just a restriction on adding that profile), and identifies the only viable mitigation as completing registrations under the Product List before the deprecation date.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: For the submission question, assuming registration content can be directly edited after 'Complete the Submission', or attempting deletion after the Publish Date, would leave incorrect registration content uncorrectable via this method. For D063816, failing to register needed additional models under the Product List before 2025/1/31 would leave those models without a valid registration path once D063816 becomes invalid (Withdrawal) on 2025/2/1.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a registration shows a deprecation/expiration warning tied to a specific profile, check whether that profile is actually needed by the product and whether it should have been removed by the original BQTF - because an unused deprecated profile left in an existing registration can cause the entire DID to become invalid on the deprecation date, not just block the addition of that profile. Also, for 'Complete the Submission' style irreversible actions, the standard correction path is delete (before Publish Date) and re-register, not direct in-place editing.
